questions.question: Which abrasive material is typically used on grinding papers or belts :

explanations.a: Incorrect — diamond is mainly used for fine polishing or very hard materials, not typically for standard grinding papers or belts.
explanations.b: Incorrect — aluminum oxide is used in some polishing stages and certain applications, but less commonly as the primary grinding paper abrasive.
explanations.c: Correct — silicon carbide (SiC) is the most commonly used abrasive for grinding papers due to its hardness and effectiveness in removing surface material.
explanations.d: Incorrect — magnesium oxide is used as a polishing agent, not for grinding papers or belts.

questions.question: Which statement regarding grit size numbers is true ?

answers.a: A 400 grit paper is coarser than an 180 grit paper.
answers.b: A 180 grit paper is coarser than a 400 grit paper
answers.c: Grit numbers only indicate the type of abrasive material.
answers.d: Grit numbers are irrelevant in the grinding process.

explanations.a: Incorrect — 400 grit is finer than 180 grit, not coarser; higher grit numbers mean smaller abrasive particles.
explanations.b: Correct — 180 grit is coarser than 400 grit because lower grit numbers indicate larger abrasive particles.
explanations.c: Incorrect — grit numbers represent particle size (coarseness/fineness), not the type of abrasive material.
explanations.d: Incorrect — grit size is very important because it controls surface roughness and preparation quality during grinding.

questions.question: Why is the specimen rotated by 90 degrees when moving from one grit size of grinding paper to the next ?

answers.a: To ensure even wear on the grinding paper
answers.b: To confuse the operator and test their attention to detail
answers.c: To see when scratches from the previous coarser grit have been completely removed
answers.d: To prevent the sample from overheating

explanations.a: Incorrect — rotating the specimen is not for grinding paper wear; it is for monitoring surface preparation quality.
explanations.b: Incorrect — it has no purpose related to operator testing or confusion.
explanations.c: Correct — rotating by 90° helps distinguish old scratches from the previous grit so you can confirm they are fully removed before moving to the next finer grit.
explanations.d: Incorrect — overheating control is managed by lubricant/cooling, not specimen rotation.

questions.question: What common problem can occur if excessive heat is generated during the initial cutting or coarse grinding stages ?

answers.a: The sample may become too difficult to handle
answers.c: The sample's internal microstructure may be altered
answers.d: The grinding machine will break down

explanations.a: Incorrect — while handling may become slightly inconvenient, it is not the primary or significant effect of overheating.
explanations.b: Incorrect — magnetization is unrelated to heat generated during cutting or grinding.
explanations.c: Correct — excessive heat can cause thermal damage such as phase changes, residual stresses, or deformation, altering the true microstructure of the sample.
explanations.d: Incorrect — machine failure is not a typical direct consequence of heat in the specimen during grinding or cutting.

questions.question: What is the general rule of thumb regarding cleanliness between different stages of sample preparation (especially when changing grit sizes) ?

answers.a: Cleanliness is not a major concern until the final step
answers.b: The sample should be thoroughly washed to prevent contamination from coarser grit particles
answers.c: Operator's hands need to be cleaned, not the sample
answers.d: Quick wipe with a dry cloth is sufficient

explanations.a: Incorrect — cleanliness is important at every stage, not only at the final step, because contamination can carry coarse particles forward and damage the surface.
explanations.b: Correct — the sample should be thoroughly cleaned between grit stages to remove coarse abrasive particles and prevent them from causing deep scratches in the next finer stage.
explanations.c: Incorrect — cleaning only hands is not enough; the specimen itself must be cleaned properly to avoid contamination.
explanations.d: Incorrect — a dry wipe is insufficient because it may leave embedded abrasive particles on the surface.

questions.question: Why is excessive pressure generally avoided during the grinding process ?

answers.a: It makes the specimen too hot to handle
answers.b: It can cause excessive material removal and waste the sample
answers.c: It can lead to change in the microstructure
answers.d: It can clog the abrasive paper too quickly

explanations.a: Incorrect — while pressure can contribute to heating, the main concern is not simply handling temperature.
explanations.b: Correct — excessive pressure can remove too much material quickly, introduce deep scratches, and unnecessarily waste the specimen surface.
explanations.c: Incorrect — pressure during grinding does not typically alter the internal microstructure; heat is the main factor for such changes.
explanations.d: Incorrect — clogging can occur, but it is not the primary reason excessive pressure is avoided.

questions.question: After the final fine grinding stage (e.g., 600 grit), what is the next major step in sample preparation ?

explanations.a: Incorrect — etching is done only after polishing to reveal microstructural features, not immediately after grinding.
explanations.b: Incorrect — microscopic observation requires a polished (and usually etched) surface, not just fine ground finish.
explanations.c: Incorrect — coarse grinding is an earlier stage used to remove cutting damage, not after fine grinding.
explanations.d: Correct — polishing is the next step after fine grinding to remove scratches and produce a smooth, mirror-like surface.
